title: Advancing Tabular Stroke Modelling Through a Novel Hybrid Architecture and Feature-Selection Synergy
summary: The paper addresses stroke prediction from a small, highly imbalanced public tabular dataset (4,981 records, ~5% stroke prevalence), arguing that single classifiers and weak preprocessing limit clinical utility. It combines IQR outlier removal, Table-2 label encoding, correlation and Random-Forest feature selection, SMOTE on the training set only, GridSearchCV over ten classifiers, and soft-voting/stacking ensembles. The headline result is a stacking ensemble reported at 97.2% accuracy, 97.15% F1-score, and 99.66% ROC-AUC, versus 91.36% accuracy for the best single model, LightGBM.

match_target.why: C1 is the paper's headline and the user's target: a CPU-cheap stacking model on ~5k tabular rows. It is not a side ablation; C2/C3 come from the same run, while C4-C7 are weaker baselines or alternate feature sets.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: no std is reported for the 97.2% accuracy; accuracy is a bounded score and the test set is 868 examples (<2,000), with the paper printing percent, so the band is ±2.0 absolute percentage points.

requirements.stmt: Use the public Full-Filled Brain Stroke Dataset with 4,981 patient records and 11 columns (10 predictors plus binary stroke target).
requirements.quote: The dataset contains records of several potential risk factors for stroke and has the target variable stroke

requirements.stmt: Encode categorical variables with the exact integer mapping in Table 2, not scikit-learn's default alphabetical LabelEncoder ordering.
requirements.quote: We employed LabelEncoder from the scikit-learn library, which assigns an integer value to each unique category.

requirements.stmt: Remove outliers from numerical features using IQR bounds Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR, reducing the dataset to 4,337 records.
requirements.cite: Section 2.3.2 Outlier Detection and Removal; Table 3
requirements.quote: After outlier removal, the dataset was reduced from 4,981 to 4,337 records

requirements.stmt: Create three feature sets: all 10 predictors, 7 correlation-selected features, and 7 Random-Forest-selected features.
requirements.quote: Full Features (all 10 predictors), Correlation-based Features (7 features selected via correlation thresholding), and Random Forest-based Features (7 features chosen based on tree-based importance)

requirements.stmt: Split each feature set 80/20 with stratification using random_state=42; the resulting test set has 868 examples.
requirements.quote: Each set was split into training (80%) and testing (20%) using stratified sampling to preserve stroke prevalence

requirements.stmt: Fit StandardScaler on the training set and apply it to numerical features only.
requirements.quote: where μ and σ represent the mean and standard deviation of each feature from the training set.

requirements.stmt: Apply SMOTE only to the training data with k=5, balancing classes to 3,312 each, and leave the test set untouched.
requirements.quote: We applied SMOTE to the training data only, ensuring that the test data remained representative of the real-world class distribution.

requirements.stmt: Tune hyperparameters with stratified 5-fold GridSearchCV, optimizing ROC-AUC.
requirements.quote: We conducted comprehensive grid searches utilizing stratified 5-fold cross-validation, focusing on optimizing for ROC-AUC to address class imbalance.

requirements.stmt: The final reported stack must use Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVC as base models with logistic regression as meta-learner.
requirements.quote: which included Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and a support-vector classifier, with logistic regression acting as a meta-learner

requirements.stmt: Build stacking meta-features from 10-fold stratified out-of-fold probability predictions to avoid leakage.
requirements.cite: Section 2.9.3 Voting and Stacking Ensemble Implementation; Equation 38
requirements.quote: meta-features were built using 10-fold stratified out-of-fold (OOF) predictions to generalize well

requirements.stmt: Use predicted class probabilities, not hard class labels, as the stacking meta-features.
requirements.quote: the out-of-fold (OOF) prediction from model j for instance i

requirements.stmt: Evaluate on the untouched 20% test set with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC.
requirements.quote: For each algorithm and feature set combination, we evaluated multiple metrics

requirements.stmt: For the final full-feature stack, use the GridSearchCV optimal settings in Table 7 for LightGBM/XGBoost (200 estimators, learning rate 0.2, max depth 7), not the illustrative Section 2.7.2 settings.
For SVC use C=1.0, RBF kernel, gamma='scale', class_weight='balanced', and probability=True.
requirements.quote: Our implementation used C = 1.0, an RBF kernel, gamma = scale (automatically adjusted based on feature variance), and class weight balancing to handle data imbalance.

requirements.stmt: Retain the stated class-imbalance handling in the base models (balanced class weight for RF/LightGBM, scale_pos_weight for XGBoost).
requirements.quote: a balanced class weight to address the imbalanced distribution of stroke versus non-stroke cases
